concepts.label: test-driven development
concepts.definition: Developing by first writing an automated test that fails, then making it pass, then refactoring the code while keeping behavior working.

concepts.label: refactoring
concepts.definition: Changing software's internal structure to make it easier to understand or cheaper to modify without changing its observable behavior.

concepts.label: design by contract
concepts.definition: Specifying explicit caller preconditions, routine postconditions and state invariants as responsibilities between software elements.

references.title: The Pragmatic Programmer
references.locator: Pragmatic Paranoia, Topic 23, Design by Contract and Implementing DBC

concepts.label: mutation testing
concepts.definition: Assessing tests by deliberately changing production code and checking whether the tests detect those changes.

concepts.label: ubiquitous language
concepts.definition: A shared, precise domain-model language used by developers and domain experts.

concepts.label: property-based testing
concepts.definition: Testing general properties over generated input domains and seeking counterexamples when a property fails.

concepts.label: accidental complexity
concepts.definition: Complexity introduced by the chosen implementation rather than inherent in the problem being solved.

references.title: The Mythical Man-Month
references.locator: Chapter 16, No Silver Bullet; Essence and Accidents

concepts.label: dead code
concepts.definition: Code or configuration that is no longer used and can be removed without losing needed behavior.

references.title: Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code

concepts.label: smoke test
concepts.definition: A small set of checks establishing that a build or deployment runs and its main functions and dependencies are available.

references.title: Continuous Delivery
references.locator: Deployment Pipeline Practices, Smoke-Test Your Deployments

concepts.label: separation of duties
concepts.definition: Assigning distinct responsibilities to different actors, including a maker and an independent checker, so one actor does not perform and approve all work.

references.title: NIST CSRC Glossary: Separation of Duty

concepts.label: deep module
concepts.definition: A module that provides substantial useful functionality through an interface requiring comparatively little knowledge to use.
concepts.scopeNote: Depth relates functionality to interface complexity, not implementation size. Interface leverage is a practitioner elaboration, not a universal workflow.

concepts.label: information hiding
concepts.definition: Organizing modules around design decisions they conceal, especially decisions likely to change, and exposing only what other modules need.
concepts.scopeNote: Private fields alone do not hide a decision if clients depend on its representation. This is not confidentiality.

references.title: David Parnas: On the Criteria To Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules

concepts.label: make illegal states unrepresentable
concepts.definition: Choosing types or data representations that exclude invalid combinations rather than merely checking for them after construction.
concepts.scopeNote: Guarantees depend on constructors, language features and escape hatches; runtime checks on an otherwise permissive representation are not the same property.

references.title: Scott Wlaschin: Making illegal states unrepresentable

concepts.label: parse, don't validate
concepts.definition: Converting less-structured input into a stronger representation that preserves established facts, instead of checking and discarding those facts.
concepts.scopeNote: Parsing includes validation; a Boolean check followed by an unchecked cast does not preserve the guarantee in the same way.

concepts.label: branded types
concepts.definition: Distinguishing values with the same underlying representation but different semantic roles so typed code cannot freely interchange them.
concepts.scopeNote: Branding alone does not validate external input or provide runtime security isolation. Nominal types, opaque types and newtypes are related, not unrestricted synonyms.

concepts.label: functional core, imperative shell
concepts.definition: Placing decisions and transformations in pure functions, with I/O and other side effects in an outer coordination layer.
concepts.scopeNote: Folder separation alone is insufficient; hidden global reads and I/O remain effects. The talk page establishes provenance; the practitioner source supplies operational detail.

concepts.label: design it twice
concepts.definition: Exploring substantially different designs and their trade-offs before committing to one.
concepts.scopeNote: A named principle attributed to Ousterhout in Pocock's guidance, not a requirement for subagents. Two reviewers or two execution attempts do not establish alternative designs.

concepts.label: characterization testing
concepts.definition: Writing tests to document what existing software actually does rather than what it ought to do.
concepts.scopeNote: Recorded behavior is not certified correct. Characterization tests may later serve as regression tests; snapshots are only one technique.

concepts.label: differential testing
concepts.definition: Giving the same inputs to implementations or versions expected to agree and investigating differences in their results.
concepts.scopeNote: A disagreement alone does not identify the faulty implementation; intentionally different specifications are not a suitable agreement oracle.

references.title: Csmith: Finding and Reporting Bugs in C Compilers

concepts.label: change-detector test
concepts.definition: A test that reproduces implementation information and reacts to implementation changes without independently checking required behavior.
concepts.scopeNote: Mocks, snapshots and interaction assertions are not automatically change detectors: an interaction can itself be required behavior. Tautological testing is related, not an exact alias.

references.title: Alex Eagle: Change-Detector Tests Considered Harmful

concepts.label: test isolation
concepts.definition: Keeping tests independent so one test's state or effects do not determine another test's outcome.
concepts.scopeNote: Serial execution is not isolation. Collaborator isolation is a different usage; isolated browser contexts do not isolate a shared database.

concepts.label: hermetic testing
concepts.definition: Running tests in a self-contained, controlled environment without assumptions about uncontrolled outside state or resources.
concepts.scopeNote: A container or one mocked request is insufficient. Hermetic tests can span multiple processes and need not be unit tests.

concepts.label: idempotency
concepts.definition: The property that repeating an operation has the same intended effect as performing it once.
concepts.scopeNote: Responses and logs may differ. This does not promise exactly-once execution; request deduplication is a possible mechanism.

concepts.label: blast radius
concepts.definition: The scope of effects or disruption that a change or failure can have, including indirect consumers and operational behavior.
concepts.scopeNote: Change-impact analysis investigates this scope; the activity and the scope are not unrestricted synonyms. A caller list is not proof of impact or safety, nor permission to expand a change.

concepts.label: ablation study
concepts.definition: Assessing a component's contribution by removing it and comparing system performance under otherwise comparable conditions.
concepts.scopeNote: Changing several factors does not isolate one contribution. No statistical significance, retraining or broad generalization is implied.

concepts.label: progressive disclosure
concepts.definition: Presenting essential information or options first and revealing secondary detail when needed.
concepts.scopeNote: Hiding essential prerequisites is not successful disclosure. Mandatory sequential steps are staged disclosure, not necessarily progressive disclosure; context-loading applications imply no measured token savings.

concepts.label: DRY
concepts.definition: Giving each piece of system knowledge one authoritative representation instead of maintaining parallel representations independently.
concepts.scopeNote: Similar-looking code can express different knowledge; textual duplication alone does not establish duplicated knowledge.

references.title: Hunt and Thomas: DRY excerpt
references.locator: DRY is More Than Code; Not All Code Duplication is Knowledge Duplication

concepts.label: YAGNI
concepts.definition: Not implementing a capability now solely because it is anticipated to be needed in the future.
concepts.scopeNote: Not a reason to neglect current testing, refactoring or design health. Avoiding speculative capabilities differs from removing unused code or unnecessary implementation complexity.

concepts.label: orthogonality
concepts.definition: Independence of aspects of a system that allows them to vary without requiring unrelated changes elsewhere.
concepts.scopeNote: Separate files alone do not establish independence. Orthogonality concerns independent variation, not merely fewer dependencies.

references.title: Hunt and Thomas: Orthogonality and the DRY Principle

concepts.label: high cohesion
concepts.definition: Grouping a coherent set of responsibilities or concepts that belong together within a module.
concepts.scopeNote: Small size or one public method alone does not establish cohesion. Cohesion concerns what belongs together, not the number of dependencies.

concepts.label: low coupling
concepts.definition: Limiting dependencies so modules can be understood and changed with relatively little knowledge of each other.
concepts.scopeNote: Zero dependencies is not the goal; splitting files can increase relationships.

concepts.label: value object
concepts.definition: A domain concept distinguished by its values rather than conceptual identity, usually with immutable behavior.
concepts.scopeNote: An immutable entity with persistent identity remains an entity; a DTO is not automatically a value object.

concepts.label: regression testing
concepts.definition: Testing after changes for unintended damage to previously working behavior.
concepts.scopeNote: Testing only a new capability is insufficient. This is not synonymous with running every test or performing a smoke test.

concepts.label: contract testing
concepts.definition: Checking that an external-service double behaves consistently with the real service for interactions consumers rely on.
concepts.scopeNote: This glossary uses the narrow service-double meaning. Schema checks may establish only part of a contract; design by contract and consumer-driven contract testing are not unrestricted aliases.

concepts.label: fuzzing
concepts.definition: Automatically exercising software with generated or mutated inputs to seek failures.
concepts.scopeNote: Mutating inputs is not production-code mutation testing. Random load without failure checks is insufficient.

concepts.label: debugging by bisection
concepts.definition: Repeatedly testing intermediate revisions between known contrasting endpoints to locate a behavior-changing revision.
concepts.scopeNote: Sequential commit testing or history reading is not bisection. Flaky or non-monotonic outcomes can mislead; git bisect is a tool, not the universal concept name.

concepts.label: optimistic concurrency control
concepts.definition: Allowing concurrent work, then validating relevant shared state before committing and rejecting or retrying conflicts.
concepts.scopeNote: Suppressing an obsolete UI response is not validating a shared-state write. Optimistic Offline Lock is a specific pattern, not an unrestricted alias.

concepts.label: expand-contract migration
concepts.definition: Expanding an interface or schema compatibly, migrating consumers, then removing the old form.
concepts.scopeNote: A one-shot rename or gradual rollout alone does not supply transitional compatibility. Independently deployed consumers can benefit; atomic internal migrations do not universally require it.

concepts.label: least privilege
concepts.definition: Giving users and processes only the privileges and resources necessary for their assigned function.
concepts.scopeNote: Limiting authority differs from assigning responsibilities to different actors, which is separation of duties.

concepts.label: Diátaxis
concepts.definition: Organizing documentation around tutorials, how-to guides, reference and explanation according to the reader’s needs.
concepts.scopeNote: Not a synonym for concise prose or diagrams, nor a rule that all four forms belong in one document.

concepts.label: anticorruption layer
concepts.definition: A translation boundary between systems with different semantic models that keeps an external or legacy model from dictating the new domain's design.
concepts.scopeNote: A generic adapter or protocol conversion without significant semantic-model differences is insufficient. Bidirectional synchronization is an additional requirement, not implied. The Microsoft explanation attributes the pattern to Eric Evans.

concepts.label: metamorphic testing
concepts.definition: Testing expected relationships between results of related executions when checking individual outputs directly is difficult.
concepts.scopeNote: Related inputs must have an expected output relationship; multiple arbitrary runs are insufficient. Related to, not synonymous with, property-based testing.

references.title: Metamorphic testing and its applications to bioinformatics

concepts.label: delta debugging
concepts.definition: Automated reduction of failure-inducing material by testing smaller candidates while preserving the failure.
concepts.scopeNote: Asking for a small reproduction alone does not establish the reduction process. Global minimality is not promised.

concepts.label: bounded context
concepts.definition: An explicit scope within which a particular domain model applies consistently.
concepts.scopeNote: Not every service, repository or deployment boundary defines a bounded context. The same word can legitimately have different meanings across contexts.

concepts.label: separation of concerns
concepts.definition: Treating distinct aspects of a problem separately so each can be reasoned about without simultaneously considering all the others.
concepts.scopeNote: Does not require a particular folder structure or architecture. Distinct from assigning responsibilities to different actors (separation of duties).

references.title: Edsger Dijkstra: On the role of scientific thought

concepts.label: backpressure
concepts.definition: Regulating upstream production of work according to downstream capacity to receive or process it.
concepts.scopeNote: Bounded worker concurrency alone is insufficient if producers keep filling an unbounded queue. The upstream response to capacity is essential.

concepts.label: exponential backoff with jitter
concepts.definition: Retrying with delays that grow exponentially, commonly up to a cap, while randomizing timing to spread retries.
concepts.scopeNote: Does not imply safe retries, a deadline or a particular jitter distribution. A fixed delay, exponential delay alone or randomness alone is insufficient.

references.title: AWS Builders’ Library: Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter

concepts.label: circuit breaker
concepts.definition: Temporarily stopping calls to a failing dependency after a failure threshold is reached, with a mechanism to test recovery before normal calls resume.
concepts.scopeNote: Distinct from retrying with longer delays or permanently disabling a feature; recovery probing need not use a particular implementation.

concepts.label: canary deployment
concepts.definition: Exposing a new release to a limited portion of production and evaluating that exposure to decide whether rollout should continue.
concepts.scopeNote: Not merely staging, a gradual rollout without evaluation, or a smoke test after full rollout. Limited exposure does not guarantee safety.

references.title: The Site Reliability Workbook: Canarying Releases

concepts.label: reconciliation loop
concepts.definition: Repeatedly comparing desired state with observed state and taking corrective action toward convergence.
concepts.scopeNote: Reporting drift without corrective action is insufficient. A loop does not guarantee instantaneous convergence or eliminate the need for safe repeated actions.

concepts.label: blinded evaluation
concepts.definition: Concealing relevant identities or conditions from evaluators to reduce identity-driven judgment bias.
concepts.scopeNote: A different-family judge or independent reviewer alone does not establish blinding. Blinding does not itself isolate a component contribution or remove every bias.
